newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's filling stations launch 24-hour strike.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's filling stations launch 24-hour strike.

text.p: Some 1,800 Moroccan filling stations on Monday went on a 24-hour strike to press demands for a rise in sales profit margins and other social benefits, a spokesman for Morocco's filling stations association said.

The Casablanca-based Federation Nationale des Commercants de Carburant au Maroc said: "We want an increase of profit margins on petrol sales to six percent from three percent and for lubricants to 25 percent from 10 percent."
Morocco has a total 2,500 filling stations including in the disputed Western Sahara territory.

"We also want the revision of contracts dating back to 1913 which make filling station managers liable to layoffs any time and prevent their children from taking over the business," the spokesman said.

Morocco, which gradually liberalised oil imports in 1995, plans to totally privatise the country's oil refineries, Samir and Societe Cherifienne des Petroles, in the first half of 1997, officials said.
With a capacity of more than 5.0 million tonnes of crude, Samir is Morocco's main oil refinery, accounting for about 80 percent of all crude imports.
Seven distribution networks for petroleum products were privatised in 1993 and 1994, and state holdings were bought by foreign firms including Mobil Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell and Total SA.
Morocco, which has no oil of its own, imports all its energy needs, mainly from the Gulf countries, including Iran.
The strike is expected to be extended if its members' demands were not satisfied, the association said.
